name: monitor
description: Portable logging + reporting workflow. Maintains a project-local monitor/ folder (Dashboard + Reports + Logs) backed by a canonical operations.mtr (schema locked in code) and a report template that evolves additively from profile.json. The Reports index has no manifest file — it's scanned fresh from reports/*.html, reading each report's own title/branch/summary out of the file. Logs and Reports are paginated statically (10 per page, plain Prev/Next links, no JS/server). Generated pages are script-free except the Dashboard, which carries one small self-contained search-box script — the single deliberate exception. Every page shows the current git branch, and each log entry and report records the branch its change was made on. Logs by default after every operation and reports by default before every merge, capturing decisions, rationale, architecture impact, next steps, and gaps so a new agent can resume cold; the policy is mirrored to persistent memory at init. A pending-state gate (monitor/.pending.json, backed by two Claude Code hooks) reminds the agent at the next turn if a commit/merge/rebase went unlogged/unreported, instead of relying on discretion alone. Report design/theme is locked to a canonical palette independent of content-tone requests (audience, reading level, language) and force-corrected on authoring via --lock-report. Commands: /monitor:init, /monitor:log, /monitor:report, /monitor:record, /monitor:search, /monitor:update, /monitor:task-start, /monitor:task-update, /monitor:task-close, /monitor:clean-logs, /monitor:clean-reports, /monitor:clean-tasks. /monitor:search covers logs, reports, and tasks, selectable with --scope. Engine is stdlib-only Python 3 with graceful fallbacks for optional companion skills. A third tracked entity, tasks (monitor/tasks/tasks.mtr), records lifecycle-tracked units of work with self-reported token/credit/cost metrics, alongside logs and reports.
